title: TokyWoky website, 2020
lede: The 2020 home page of a French community-platform startup: small flat figures with long legs gather on a grey platform in front of an oversized browser window.
summary: Small long-legged flat figures around a giant tilted browser window, next to a bold blue heading. 2020.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 and inspected. No cookie box covers the page. Wayback redirected to a copy without the `if_` flag, but no archive toolbar appears in the screenshot. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens.

styles.note: Borderline: long-legged figures with small heads act around an oversized interface, the style’s standard scene, but the skin is natural and the platform and screen use soft gradients.

context: The live address now redirects to a Skeepers brand-community page, which returned “Error 403 Forbidden” to `tools/capture.mjs` on 28 September 2026.
observed: The heading “Go from website to community” is set in a heavy bright blue sans-serif, with grey body text and a pill-shaped blue button “REQUEST A DEMO”.
On the right, a large tilted browser window in light grey shows a red-framed portrait and grey text bars.
Seven small figures stand around it on a grey oval platform: they hold star-rating cards, speech bubbles with “?” and “!”, and a phone.
The figures have small heads, long thin legs, and dark clothes; skin tones are natural. Teal plant shapes stand behind them.
The window and the platform have soft grey gradients and cast shadows.
interpretation: The scene is the style’s most common product layout: many small people acting on one giant screen. The gradients and shadows mix it with the soft 3D of later SaaS illustration.
borrow: Show a platform with many small figures each doing one different action around the product screen, to suggest a community.

images.alt: TokyWoky home page, 2020: the bold blue heading “Go from website to community” on the left and seven small long-legged figures holding rating cards and speech bubbles around a giant tilted browser window on the right.
